    90	
    91	# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
    92	mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
    93	export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    94	export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
    95	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
    96	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
    97	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
    98	export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
    99	export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
   100	unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
   101	
   102	LOG="$WORK/step.log"
   103	run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
   104	  local desc="$1"; shift
   105	  if ! "$@" > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
   106	    cat "$LOG" >&2
   107	    die3 "$desc"
   108	  fi
   109	}
   110	
   111	suffix=""
   112	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"

   114	echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"
   115	
   116	# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
   117	UP="$WORK/upstream"
   118	run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
   119	run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
   120	run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
   121	
   122	overlay() {
   123	  local p
   124	  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
   125	    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
   126	      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
   127	      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
   128	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   129	      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
   130	    else
   131	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   132	    fi
   133	  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)

   135	  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
   136	}
   137	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
   138	MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
   139	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"
   140	
   141	# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
   142	DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
   143	mkdir -p "$DOWN"
   144	init_downstream() {
   145	  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
   146	  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
   147	  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
   148	  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
   149	}
   150	run_step "downstream init" init_downstream
   151	
   152	do_mount() {
   153	  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
   154	    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
   155	}
   156	run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
   157	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"
   158	
   159	# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
   160	CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"
   161	[[ -f "$CFG" ]] || : > "$CFG"
   162	if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   163	  run_step "aleph.enabled: false" yq -i '.aleph.enabled = false' "$CFG"
   164	else
   165	  printf '\naleph:\n  enabled: false\n' >> "$CFG"
   166	fi
   167	
   168	# --- 4. check-loa.sh ------------------------------------------------------------
   169	OUT="$WORK/check-loa.out"
   170	rc=0
   171	(cd "$DOWN" && CI=true bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh < /dev/null) > "$OUT" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   172	echo "----- check-loa.sh (downstream) -----"
   173	cat "$OUT"
   174	echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
   175	
   176	tampered=$(grep -c 'Tampered: ' "$OUT" || true)
   177	missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
   178	not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")

   181	exit 1

     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,

    11	#

    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.

    26	# Usage:

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
     6	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
     7	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
     8	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
     9	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
    10	#
    11	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
    12	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
    13	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
    14	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
    15	#                      (a path component of that name)
    16	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
    17	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
    18	#                  other
    19	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
    20	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
    21	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
    22	#
    23	# Last line on stdout:
    24	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
    28	#
    29	# Options:
    30	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
    31	#                    current directory)
    32	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
    33	#   -h, --help       this text
    34	#
    35	# Exit codes:
    36	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
    37	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
    38	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
    39	#      not JSON with a `files` object
    40	# =============================================================================
    41	set -euo pipefail
    42	export LC_ALL=C
    43	
    44	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    45	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	
    47	ROOT=""
    48	MANIFEST=""
    49	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    50	  case "$1" in
    51	    --root)
    52	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    53	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    54	    --manifest)
    55	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
    56	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    58	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    59	  esac
    60	done
    61	
    62	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    63	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    64	fi
    65	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    66	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    67	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    68	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    69	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
    70	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
    71	jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$MANIFEST" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    72	  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
    73	
    74	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
    75	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    76	trap cleanup EXIT
    77	
    78	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
    79	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
    80	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
    81	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
    82	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
    83	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
    84	
    85	classify() {
    86	  local p="$1"
    87	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
    88	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    89	  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
    90	    printf '.pyc'
    91	  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
    92	    printf '.lock'
    93	  else
    94	    printf 'other'
    95	  fi
    96	}
    97	
    98	# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
    99	: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   100	while IFS= read -r p; do
   101	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   102	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   103	done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   104	
   105	: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   106	while IFS= read -r p; do
   107	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   108	  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   109	done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   110	
   111	entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
   112	n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
   113	n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
   114	
   115	class_summary=""
   116	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
   117	  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
   118	  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
   119	    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
   120	    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
   121	    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
   122	    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
   123	    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
   124	  done
   125	fi
   126	if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   127	  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
   128	  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
   129	fi
   130	
   131	echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
   132	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   133	  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   134	  exit 1
   135	fi
   136	exit 0
===== fresh-mount-proof.sh
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
     4	#
     5	# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
     6	# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
     7	# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
     8	#
     9	# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
    10	#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
    11	#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
    12	#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
    13	#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
    14	#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
    15	#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
    16	#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
    17	#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
    18	#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
    19	#                    submodule from there; no network).
    20	#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
    21	#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
    22	#      is printed, then a summary line
    23	#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
    24	#
    25	# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
    26	# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
    27	# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
    28	#
    29	# Usage:
    30	#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
    31	#
    32	# Options:
    33	#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
    34	#                repository the script lives in)
    35	#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
    36	#                (use before the change is committed)
    37	#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
    38	#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
    39	#                /tmp)
    40	#   -h, --help   this text
    41	#
    42	# Exit codes:
    43	#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
    44	#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
    45	#   2    usage error
    46	#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
    47	#        the failing step's output is printed
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    53	die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
    55	
    56	REF=""
    57	KEEP=0
    58	WORKTREE=0
    59	TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --ref)
    63	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
    64	      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    65	    --tmp)
    66	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
    67	      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    68	    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    69	    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
    70	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    71	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    72	  esac
    73	done
    74	[[ -d "$TMP_PARENT" ]] || die2 "--tmp is not a directory: $TMP_PARENT"
    75	
    76	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
    77	SRC="$(git -C "$SELF_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "script is not inside a git work tree"
    78	[[ -n "$REF" ]] || REF="HEAD"
    79	REF_SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REF}^{commit}")" || die2 "not a commit in $SRC: $REF"
    80	
    81	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
    82	cleanup() {
    83	  if [[ $KEEP -eq 1 ]]; then
    84	    echo "fresh-mount-proof: kept $WORK" >&2
    85	  else
    86	    rm -rf "$WORK"
    87	  fi
    88	}
    89	trap cleanup EXIT
    90	
    91	# --- hermetic git ---------------------------------------------------------------
    92	mkdir -p "$WORK/no-hooks"
    93	export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
    94	export GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=3
    95	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=protocol.file.allow GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=always
    96	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1="$WORK/no-hooks"
    97	export GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2=init.defaultBranch GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2=main
    98	export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="fresh-mount-proof" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="fresh-mount-proof@localhost"
    99	export GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="$GIT_AUTHOR_NAME" GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="$GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL"
   100	unset LOA_ALEPH_ENABLED
   101	
   102	LOG="$WORK/step.log"
   103	run_step() {  # run_step <description> <cmd...>; output to $LOG, printed on failure
   104	  local desc="$1"; shift
   105	  if ! "$@" > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
   106	    cat "$LOG" >&2
   107	    die3 "$desc"
   108	  fi
   109	}
   110	
   111	suffix=""
   112	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && suffix=" + work-tree state"
   113	echo "fresh-mount-proof: source $SRC at ${REF_SHA}${suffix}"
   114	echo "fresh-mount-proof: temp dir $WORK"
   115	
   116	# --- 1. upstream clone ----------------------------------------------------------
   117	UP="$WORK/upstream"
   118	run_step "clone $SRC" git clone --quiet --no-checkout "file://$SRC" "$UP"
   119	run_step "fetch $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" fetch --quiet origin "$REF_SHA"
   120	run_step "branch at $REF_SHA" git -C "$UP" checkout --quiet -B fresh-mount-proof "$REF_SHA"
   121	
   122	overlay() {
   123	  local p
   124	  while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do
   125	    if [[ -e "$SRC/$p" || -L "$SRC/$p" ]]; then
   126	      [[ -d "$SRC/$p" && ! -L "$SRC/$p" ]] && continue   # gitlink / nested repo
   127	      mkdir -p "$UP/$(dirname "$p")"
   128	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   129	      cp -P "$SRC/$p" "$UP/$p"
   130	    else
   131	      rm -f "$UP/$p"
   132	    fi
   133	  done < <(git -C "$SRC" ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard)
   134	  git -C "$UP" add -A
   135	  git -C "$UP" commit --quiet --allow-empty -m "fresh-mount-proof: work-tree state of $SRC"
   136	}
   137	[[ $WORKTREE -eq 1 ]] && run_step "work-tree overlay" overlay
   138	MOUNT_SHA="$(git -C "$UP" rev-parse HEAD)"
   139	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mounting upstream commit $MOUNT_SHA"
   140	
   141	# --- 2. downstream repository and the submodule mount --------------------------
   142	DOWN="$WORK/downstream"
   143	mkdir -p "$DOWN"
   144	init_downstream() {
   145	  git -C "$DOWN" init --quiet
   146	  printf '# downstream fixture\n' > "$DOWN/README.md"
   147	  git -C "$DOWN" add README.md
   148	  git -C "$DOWN" commit --quiet -m "initial commit"
   149	}
   150	run_step "downstream init" init_downstream
   151	
   152	do_mount() {
   153	  (cd "$DOWN" && LOA_UPSTREAM="file://$UP" bash "$UP/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh" \
   154	    --branch fresh-mount-proof --ref "$MOUNT_SHA" --force < /dev/null)
   155	}
   156	run_step "mount-submodule.sh" do_mount
   157	echo "fresh-mount-proof: mount-submodule.sh exited 0 ($(grep -c 'Linked' "$LOG" || true) link lines)"
   158	
   159	# --- 3. Aleph off ---------------------------------------------------------------
   160	CFG="$DOWN/.loa.config.yaml"
   161	[[ -f "$CFG" ]] || : > "$CFG"
   162	if command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   163	  run_step "aleph.enabled: false" yq -i '.aleph.enabled = false' "$CFG"
   164	else
   165	  printf '\naleph:\n  enabled: false\n' >> "$CFG"
   166	fi
   167	
   168	# --- 4. check-loa.sh ------------------------------------------------------------
   169	OUT="$WORK/check-loa.out"
   170	rc=0
   171	(cd "$DOWN" && CI=true bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh < /dev/null) > "$OUT" 2>&1 || rc=$?
   172	echo "----- check-loa.sh (downstream) -----"
   173	cat "$OUT"
   174	echo "----- end check-loa.sh (exit $rc) -----"
   175	
   176	tampered=$(grep -c 'Tampered: ' "$OUT" || true)
   177	missing=$(grep -c 'Missing: ' "$OUT" || true)
   178	not_mounted=$(sed -n 's/.*not-mounted: \([0-9][0-9]*\) path(s).*/\1/p' "$OUT")
   179	echo "fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=${tampered} Missing=${missing} not-mounted=${not_mounted:-0} check-loa-rc=${rc}"
   180	[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && exit 0
   181	exit 1

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
     4	#
     5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
     9	#
    10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
    11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
    12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
    13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
    14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
    15	#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
    16	#
    17	# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
    18	#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
    19	#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
    20	#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
    21	#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
    22	#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
    23	#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
    24	#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
    25	#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
    26	#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
    27	#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
    28	#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
    29	#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
    30	#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
    31	#      bats | bash | node | npx
    32	#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src

# Beads Workflow (beads_rust) — auditing-security

Referenced from `auditing-security/SKILL.md` `<beads_workflow>`.

When `br` is installed: `br sync --import-only` at session start, `br sync --flush-only` at session end. Record the result:

```bash
br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
br label add <task-id> security
# then exactly one of:
# If approved
br label add <task-id> security-approved
# If changes required
br label add <task-id> security-blocked
```
A re-review or re-audit adds its round's label and `br label add` never removes the other, so a task can carry both: the latest `SECURITY AUDIT:` comment is the verdict of record (with the feedback file and the COMPLETED marker), a label only history.

Log a discovered vulnerability as its own issue: `.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh "<sprint-epic-id>" "Security: <criterion> (see auditor-sprint-feedback.md)" bug 0` — the criterion only, never the finding text or its file (the flushed JSONL is committed; the location stays in the feedback file), then `br label add <new-issue-id> security`. Protocol: `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`.

### Agent Teams
A teammate runs no `br` command: it reports the result to the lead via SendMessage, and the lead runs it. A comment carries the verdict and the feedback file's path only — never finding text or code.

# Audit Rubrics

Structured evaluation rubrics for each audit category. Use these to score findings consistently.

## How to Use

1. For each dimension, assess the codebase against the criteria
2. Assign score 1-5 based on the rubric
3. Record reasoning trace explaining the score
4. Calculate category average for overall health

---

## Security Rubrics

### SEC-IV: Input Validation
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | All inputs validated, sanitized, and typed. Allowlist approach used. Schema validation on APIs. |
| 4 | Most inputs validated with minor gaps. Edge cases may lack validation. |
| 3 | Basic validation present but incomplete. Some injection risks remain. |
| 2 | Minimal validation. Clear injection vulnerabilities exist. |
| 1 | No input validation. User input flows directly to sensitive operations. |

### SEC-AZ: Authorization
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | RBAC/ABAC properly implemented. All routes protected. Least privilege enforced. |
| 4 | Authorization present with minor gaps (some routes missing checks). |
| 3 | Basic auth checks but inconsistent. Privilege escalation may be possible. |
| 2 | Weak authorization. Easy bypass or missing on critical routes. |
| 1 | No authorization or completely broken access control. |

### SEC-CI: Confidentiality/Integrity
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Encryption at rest and in transit. Proper key management. Data classified and protected. |
| 4 | Good encryption with minor gaps. Some sensitive data handling could improve. |
| 3 | Basic encryption but inconsistent. Some data exposure risks. |
| 2 | Weak or missing encryption. Sensitive data partially exposed. |
| 1 | No encryption. Sensitive data in plaintext. Secrets in code. |

### SEC-IN: Injection Prevention
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Parameterized queries everywhere. No string concatenation in queries. ORM used safely. |
| 4 | Mostly safe with minor gaps in edge cases. |
| 3 | Mixed usage. Some queries parameterized, others vulnerable. |
| 2 | Frequent string concatenation in queries. Clear SQL/NoSQL injection paths. |
| 1 | Pervasive injection vulnerabilities. Eval/exec with user input. |

### SEC-AV: Availability/Resilience
| Score | Criteria |
|-------|----------|
| 5 | Rate limiting, circuit breakers, graceful degradation. DoS protection in place. |
| 4 | Good availability measures with minor gaps. |
| 3 | Basic rate limiting but incomplete. Some DoS vectors remain. |
| 2 | Minimal protection. Resource exhaustion possible. |
| 1 | No availability protection. Trivial DoS attacks possible. |

===== verdict-derive help
Usage: verdict-derive.sh --file <feedback.md> --gate review|audit [--json] [--require-trailer] [--envelope <adversarial-<gate>.json>]
       [--review-file <engineer-feedback.md>]

Derive and validate the LOA-VERDICT machine trailer (C6) on a review/audit
feedback file.

Options:
  --file PATH         Feedback file to check (required)
  --gate review|audit Which gate this file belongs to (required)
  --json              Emit a JSON result object to stdout
  --require-trailer   Treat a missing trailer as a violation (exit 1) instead
                       of the default legacy-file pass (exit 2)
  --envelope <path>   The dissent envelope for the rejected-payload contract (default: adversarial-<gate>.json
                      beside --file). Rejected sidecar rows count too: the files the envelope lists in
                      metadata.rejected_sidecars always count, and so does a non-empty unlisted
                      adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl beside the envelope (with a warning naming it: an
                      earlier run's rows that were never folded); without an envelope, or without that field,
                      every adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl beside it counts; a pre-FR-2 envelope (no
                      metadata.rejected_summary key and none of rejected_sidecars or companion_voice —
                      rejected_count is no marker, the writer before cycle-126 set it too) counts none of the
                      rows as old as itself, while a sidecar newer than it counts, with a warning
                      (one git tracks with its committed bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout
                      gave it); one top-level bullet per rejected payload
                      under '## Rejected dissent payloads'; a missing explicit path is a usage error (exit 1).
                      A moved-aside adversarial-<gate>.json.prev or adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl.prev
                      with no envelope is a violation (dissent_aborted: the run never wrote its envelope).
  --review-file PATH  Audit gate only: cross-check the audit trailer's
                       excluded_confirmed against the review trailer's excluded
  -h, --help          Show this help message

Coverage-first rule (FR-9, additive): the trailer may carry "excluded": N —
the number of HIGH findings the reviewer demoted to "## Observations" because
they are tagged speculative with confidence: low. critical is never excludable;
a HIGH under ## Observations needs both markers; N must equal what the section
holds. An audit trailer carries "excluded_confirmed": N and must match.

Exit codes:
  0  trailer present and consistent
  1  trailer present but inconsistent (repair text on stderr), a usage
     error, or a missing trailer with --require-trailer set

# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= pr/PR.md)
**Change under audit:** `pr/head.diff` (72 files; cycle-130 sprint-258 — mount integrity #1267, spend caps, ablation suite and arms, container pipeline executor, rows and took-effect evidence, smoke)

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The change adds a container-based pipeline executor (`evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh`, 907 lines, new) that runs an untrusted agent session with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` inside `docker run --read-only --pids-limit --memory` with exactly two bind mounts, a sandbox materialiser (`lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, new), the row builder, took-effect prover, spend scripts, the integrity tooling for #1267 and two edits to the System Zone fences (`preflight.sh`, `check-loa.sh`). I read every head-side script, the Dockerfile, the workflow, the suite file and the bats suites; ran the security dissent on `pr/head.diff` (two voices, 2/2 succeeded, 0 rejected payloads); and reproduced the two mechanisms behind the HIGH findings on this host (git 2.39.5, jq 1.6).

The secret-handling design is strong: credentials travel in the environment only, through a `python3 -I` exec shim that closes descriptors and keeps an allowlist; every capture masks `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` as `<set>` (`pipeline-run.sh:620-632, 702-710`); the per-run HOME is removed on the EXIT trap and on signals (`:348, :356`); no `eval` anywhere; every jq program takes `--arg`. Leak guards refuse `hidden`, defect keys and arm ids before a phase runs (`:502-521`).

Four findings block the merge. One is new to this audit and is the most serious: the containment boundary the executor is built around has a hole on the host side. After IMPLEMENT and FIX the driver runs `git add -A` and `git commit` **on the host** against `sandbox/.git`, a directory the containerised agent writes freely. Git executes repo-local hooks and `core.fsmonitor` / `core.hooksPath` / filter commands from that `.git`; `env -i` with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` does not isolate repo-local config. I confirmed on this host that both a planted `pre-commit` hook and a `core.fsmonitor` command run under the exact `sgit` invocation. The same PR gets this right elsewhere: `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:96` pins `core.hooksPath` to an empty directory for its hermetic git. The other three confirm the review's blocking findings (jq 1.6 keyword `label`; preflight's count no longer looks at the disk; `check-loa.sh` cannot see a removed link in a submodule mount), each re-verified here.

Pre-flight note: Phase 0 of this skill expects `engineer-feedback.md` to read "All good"; it reads CHANGES_REQUIRED (0/3/6/11). The task instruction ordered the audit regardless, so I proceeded and record the deviation here. `adversarial-review.json` carries `metadata.model` (gate satisfied). Beads (`br`) is not installed; the beads steps are skipped.

**Security Issues Found:**
| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 4 |

### [HIGH-001] Host-side git on an agent-writable `.git` executes sandbox-planted hooks and config commands on the host

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high — mechanism reproduced; exploitation needs the agent, or content that steers it, to write into `sandbox/.git`)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:783` (also `:784`, `:787`; the wrapper at `:446-449`)
**Issue:** `sgit` is
```bash
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$META" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 LC_ALL=C \
  git -C "$WS" "$@"
```
and after every IMPLEMENT/FIX phase `run_phase` calls `sgit add -A`, `sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label"` and `sgit bundle create …` (`:783-787`). `$WS/.git` sits inside `/workspace`, the read-write bind mount the agent session owns (`:689`), so the agent (running `--dangerously-skip-permissions` with `Bash`, `:651-653`) or any `.claude/` hook of the mounted tree can write `sandbox/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `sandbox/.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `filter.*.clean`, `gpg.program` with `commit.gpgsign=true`) before the host-side commit. `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` / `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` suppress the global and system files only; repo-local config and `.git/hooks` are read as usual.
**Reproduced here** (git 2.39.5): a repo with `.git/hooks/pre-commit` touching a marker and `core.fsmonitor` set to a `touch` command, then exactly the `sgit` environment running `git add -A` and `git commit --allow-empty`: both markers were created on the host.
**Impact:** Code execution on the operator host as the operator (`--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` means the host uid; the operator's `~/.codex/auth.json`, `~/.aws`, SSH keys and the batch results are all reachable), bypassing `--read-only`, `--pids-limit`, `--memory` and the two-mount rule (DEC-0411) that exist to contain exactly this agent. Review-catch fixtures carry third-party PR text, so the steering content need not be the operator's own.
**Fix:** Never run git on the host against a `.git` the sandbox can write. Either keep the snapshot repository outside the mount — `git --git-dir="$META/snap.git" --work-tree="$WS"` for init/base/add/commit/bundle (and give the sandbox its own `.git` for the gates' `git diff $BASE_COMMIT`, created from the same base) — or, at minimum, pass explicit overrides on every `sgit` call: `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.sshCommand=false` and clear filter/diff drivers, as `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:92-96` already does with `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath`. Prefer the separate `--git-dir`: an allowlist of config keys is a moving target. Add a bats case that plants a `pre-commit` hook in the stub sandbox and asserts it did not run.
**Reference:** CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html; CWE-250 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/250.html; OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration — https://owasp.org/Top10/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/

### [HIGH-002] jq keyword `label` breaks the executor, the mount library and the row builder on jq 1.6 (review §1, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:702` (also `:816`, `:881`), `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462-467`, `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285`
**Issue:** `jq -n --arg label "$label" … '{label: $label, …}'` and the shorthand `{name, label, …}`. `label` is a jq reserved word; jq 1.6 (Debian 12 bookworm — the lineage `Dockerfile.ablation:22` pins — and Ubuntu 22.04) rejects both. Reproduced on this host:
```
$ jq -nc --arg label x '{l: $label}'
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__
$ echo '{"label":1}' | jq -c '{label}'
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected '}', expecting ':'
```
Under `set -e` the argv capture at `:702` aborts `run_phase` and every run ends `infrastructure_error` before its first phase; `write_sandbox_grimoire` returns 2 for every mounted arm (`sandbox-mount.sh:468-469` → `pipeline-run.sh:488`); `ablation-row.sh` exits 3 (undocumented) for every `--run-dir`. CI runs on `ubuntu-latest` (jq 1.7.1) and cannot see it. The repository declares no jq minimum.
**Fix:** Rename the bindings (`--arg lbl "$label"` / `$lbl`) at `pipeline-run.sh:702, 816, 881` and `sandbox-mount.sh:462`; expand `ablation-row.sh:285` to `label: .label`. Add a CI leg on `ubuntu-22.04` or a bats case that runs one program from each script under a jq 1.6 binary when present.
**Reference:** jq 1.7 changelog, "Allow keywords to be used as binding name and in object construction".

### [HIGH-003] preflight's integrity count is an index count and no longer sees the disk (review §2 + dissent DISS-C-003, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:189-191` (fallback `:195-197`, decision `:199-214`)
**Issue:**
```bash
ACTUAL_COUNT=$(git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" ls-files -- .claude \
    | awk '!/^\.claude\/overrides\// && $0 != ".claude/checksums.json"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
```
`git ls-files` counts index entries. Deleting a tracked hook from the working tree (`rm .claude/hooks/<gate>.sh`) does not change it, and neither does planting an untracked file under `.claude/` (a new skill or command is auto-discovered by the CLI). Both cases change the pre-PR `find … -type f` count, which now runs only when the tracked count is zero. The manifest is itself generated from `git ls-files` (`tools/gen-checksums.sh:102`), so index-vs-manifest is a tautology for the one thing a count can detect. In `integrity_enforcement: strict` this is the only fence that exits non-zero before an operation.
**Fix:** Count tracked paths that exist (`[[ -f "$MANIFEST_TREE/$p" ]]` filter, or subtract `git ls-files --deleted -- .claude`) and add the untracked set (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- .claude`) to the comparison, or do the sha256 verification the comment at `:175` already concedes is the real check. Bats cases: delete one tracked file → warning and `exit 1` under strict; plant one untracked file → same.
**Reference:** CWE-354 Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/354.html

### [HIGH-004] `not-mounted` in a submodule mount cannot distinguish a never-linked path from a removed link (review §3 + dissent DISS-C-001, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: medium — requires a submodule mount; the design is as the comment at `:47-55` describes)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75-76` (summary `:83-85`)
**Issue:**
```bash
elif [[ "$submodule_mount" == "true" && -f ".loa/${file}" ]]; then
  not_mounted=$((not_mounted + 1))
```
Every path the mount links exists under `.loa/` by construction, so in a submodule mount deleting any linked hook, rule or script is counted as informational `not-mounted` and the run prints `Integrity verified` with exit 0, where it was `Missing` (fail) before. `mount-submodule.sh` logs `Linked: …` lines (`:908-965`) but persists no link set, so the classifier has nothing to compare against; the summary prints a count, not the paths. The only tamper signal left in that mode is a hash mismatch on a file that is still present.
**Fix:** Persist the linked set at mount time (`.loa-version.json` `linked: [...]` or `.claude/.mount-links`) and classify an absent path as `Missing` when it is in that set, `not-mounted` otherwise. Until then print the not-mounted paths and add a `check-loa-mount-scope.bats` case that removes a linked file and asserts a failure.
**Reference:** CWE-354 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/354.html; OWASP ASVS V14.2 — https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/

The change adds a container-based pipeline executor (`evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh`, 907 lines, new) that runs an untrusted agent session with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` inside `docker run --read-only --pids-limit --memory` with exactly two bind mounts, a sandbox materialiser (`lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, new), the row builder, took-effect prover, spend scripts, the integrity tooling for #1267 and two edits to the System Zone fences (`preflight.sh`, `check-loa.sh`). I read every head-side script, the Dockerfile, the workflow, the suite file and the bats suites; ran the security dissent on `pr/head.diff` (two voices, 2/2 succeeded, 0 rejected payloads); and reproduced the two mechanisms behind the HIGH findings on this host (git 2.39.5, jq 1.6).

The secret-handling design is strong: credentials travel in the environment only, through a `python3 -I` exec shim that closes descriptors and keeps an allowlist; every capture masks `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` as `<set>` (`pipeline-run.sh:620-632, 702-710`); the per-run HOME is removed on the EXIT trap and on signals (`:348, :356`); no `eval` anywhere; every jq program takes `--arg`. Leak guards refuse `hidden`, defect keys and arm ids before a phase runs (`:502-521`).

Four findings block the merge. One is new to this audit and is the most serious: the containment boundary the executor is built around has a hole on the host side. After IMPLEMENT and FIX the driver runs `git add -A` and `git commit` **on the host** against `sandbox/.git`, a directory the containerised agent writes freely. Git executes repo-local hooks and `core.fsmonitor` / `core.hooksPath` / filter commands from that `.git`; `env -i` with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` does not isolate repo-local config. I confirmed on this host that both a planted `pre-commit` hook and a `core.fsmonitor` command run under the exact `sgit` invocation. The same PR gets this right elsewhere: `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:96` pins `core.hooksPath` to an empty directory for its hermetic git. The other three confirm the review's blocking findings (jq 1.6 keyword `label`; preflight's count no longer looks at the disk; `check-loa.sh` cannot see a removed link in a submodule mount), each re-verified here.

Pre-flight note: Phase 0 of this skill expects `engineer-feedback.md` to read "All good"; it reads CHANGES_REQUIRED (0/3/6/11). The task instruction ordered the audit regardless, so I proceeded and record the deviation here. `adversarial-review.json` carries `metadata.model` (gate satisfied). Beads (`br`) is not installed; the beads steps are skipped.

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] Host-side git on an agent-writable `.git` executes sandbox-planted hooks and config commands on the host

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high — mechanism reproduced; exploitation needs the agent, or content that steers it, to write into `sandbox/.git`)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:783` (also `:784`, `:787`; the wrapper at `:446-449`)
**Issue:** `sgit` is
```bash
env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$META" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 LC_ALL=C \
  git -C "$WS" "$@"
```
and after every IMPLEMENT/FIX phase `run_phase` calls `sgit add -A`, `sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label"` and `sgit bundle create …` (`:783-787`). `$WS/.git` sits inside `/workspace`, the read-write bind mount the agent session owns (`:689`), so the agent (running `--dangerously-skip-permissions` with `Bash`, `:651-653`) or any `.claude/` hook of the mounted tree can write `sandbox/.git/hooks/pre-commit`, `sandbox/.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `filter.*.clean`, `gpg.program` with `commit.gpgsign=true`) before the host-side commit. `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` / `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` suppress the global and system files only; repo-local config and `.git/hooks` are read as usual.
**Reproduced here** (git 2.39.5): a repo with `.git/hooks/pre-commit` touching a marker and `core.fsmonitor` set to a `touch` command, then exactly the `sgit` environment running `git add -A` and `git commit --allow-empty`: both markers were created on the host.
**Impact:** Code execution on the operator host as the operator (`--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"` means the host uid; the operator's `~/.codex/auth.json`, `~/.aws`, SSH keys and the batch results are all reachable), bypassing `--read-only`, `--pids-limit`, `--memory` and the two-mount rule (DEC-0411) that exist to contain exactly this agent. Review-catch fixtures carry third-party PR text, so the steering content need not be the operator's own.
**Fix:** Never run git on the host against a `.git` the sandbox can write. Either keep the snapshot repository outside the mount — `git --git-dir="$META/snap.git" --work-tree="$WS"` for init/base/add/commit/bundle (and give the sandbox its own `.git` for the gates' `git diff $BASE_COMMIT`, created from the same base) — or, at minimum, pass explicit overrides on every `sgit` call: `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c commit.gpgsign=false -c core.sshCommand=false` and clear filter/diff drivers, as `tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:92-96` already does with `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1=core.hooksPath`. Prefer the separate `--git-dir`: an allowlist of config keys is a moving target. Add a bats case that plants a `pre-commit` hook in the stub sandbox and asserts it did not run.
**Reference:** CWE-829 Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html; CWE-250 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/250.html; OWASP A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration — https://owasp.org/Top10/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/

### [HIGH-002] jq keyword `label` breaks the executor, the mount library and the row builder on jq 1.6 (review §1, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:702` (also `:816`, `:881`), `head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462-467`, `head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:285`
**Issue:** `jq -n --arg label "$label" … '{label: $label, …}'` and the shorthand `{name, label, …}`. `label` is a jq reserved word; jq 1.6 (Debian 12 bookworm — the lineage `Dockerfile.ablation:22` pins — and Ubuntu 22.04) rejects both. Reproduced on this host:
```
$ jq -nc --arg label x '{l: $label}'
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected label, expecting IDENT or __loc__
$ echo '{"label":1}' | jq -c '{label}'
jq: error: syntax error, unexpected '}', expecting ':'
```
Under `set -e` the argv capture at `:702` aborts `run_phase` and every run ends `infrastructure_error` before its first phase; `write_sandbox_grimoire` returns 2 for every mounted arm (`sandbox-mount.sh:468-469` → `pipeline-run.sh:488`); `ablation-row.sh` exits 3 (undocumented) for every `--run-dir`. CI runs on `ubuntu-latest` (jq 1.7.1) and cannot see it. The repository declares no jq minimum.
**Fix:** Rename the bindings (`--arg lbl "$label"` / `$lbl`) at `pipeline-run.sh:702, 816, 881` and `sandbox-mount.sh:462`; expand `ablation-row.sh:285` to `label: .label`. Add a CI leg on `ubuntu-22.04` or a bats case that runs one program from each script under a jq 1.6 binary when present.
**Reference:** jq 1.7 changelog, "Allow keywords to be used as binding name and in object construction".

### [HIGH-003] preflight's integrity count is an index count and no longer sees the disk (review §2 + dissent DISS-C-003, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/preflight.sh:189-191` (fallback `:195-197`, decision `:199-214`)
**Issue:**
```bash
ACTUAL_COUNT=$(git -C "${MANIFEST_TREE}" ls-files -- .claude \
    | awk '!/^\.claude\/overrides\// && $0 != ".claude/checksums.json"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
```
`git ls-files` counts index entries. Deleting a tracked hook from the working tree (`rm .claude/hooks/<gate>.sh`) does not change it, and neither does planting an untracked file under `.claude/` (a new skill or command is auto-discovered by the CLI). Both cases change the pre-PR `find … -type f` count, which now runs only when the tracked count is zero. The manifest is itself generated from `git ls-files` (`tools/gen-checksums.sh:102`), so index-vs-manifest is a tautology for the one thing a count can detect. In `integrity_enforcement: strict` this is the only fence that exits non-zero before an operation.
**Fix:** Count tracked paths that exist (`[[ -f "$MANIFEST_TREE/$p" ]]` filter, or subtract `git ls-files --deleted -- .claude`) and add the untracked set (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- .claude`) to the comparison, or do the sha256 verification the comment at `:175` already concedes is the real check. Bats cases: delete one tracked file → warning and `exit 1` under strict; plant one untracked file → same.
**Reference:** CWE-354 Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/354.html

### [HIGH-004] `not-mounted` in a submodule mount cannot distinguish a never-linked path from a removed link (review §3 + dissent DISS-C-001, confirmed)

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: medium — requires a submodule mount; the design is as the comment at `:47-55` describes)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:75-76` (summary `:83-85`)
**Issue:**
```bash
elif [[ "$submodule_mount" == "true" && -f ".loa/${file}" ]]; then
  not_mounted=$((not_mounted + 1))
```
Every path the mount links exists under `.loa/` by construction, so in a submodule mount deleting any linked hook, rule or script is counted as informational `not-mounted` and the run prints `Integrity verified` with exit 0, where it was `Missing` (fail) before. `mount-submodule.sh` logs `Linked: …` lines (`:908-965`) but persists no link set, so the classifier has nothing to compare against; the summary prints a count, not the paths. The only tamper signal left in that mode is a hash mismatch on a file that is still present.
**Fix:** Persist the linked set at mount time (`.loa-version.json` `linked: [...]` or `.claude/.mount-links`) and classify an absent path as `Missing` when it is in that set, `not-mounted` otherwise. Until then print the not-mounted paths and add a `check-loa-mount-scope.bats` case that removes a linked file and asserts a failure.
**Reference:** CWE-354 — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/354.html; OWASP ASVS V14.2 — https://owasp.org/www-project-application-security-verification-standard/

## Medium/Low Priority Issues

### [MED-001] Operator credential copies in the run directory outlive the run when the driver is killed
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium)
- **File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:569-571` (cleanup `:348`, `:356`; header `:104-106`)
- **Issue:** `make_home` copies `$CREDS_HOME/.codex/auth.json` and `config.toml` (the operator's codex OAuth tokens) into `<run>/meta/home/.codex/`, which is then bind-mounted read-write at `/home/evaluser` (`:690`). Removal happens only in `finish` and the EXIT trap. The header itself plans for a SIGKILLed driver (`:105-106`, "rewritten with status running after each phase so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a record") and `ablation-row.sh` reads `running` as interrupted — in exactly that case the live token file stays in the run directory that the batch runner, the row builder and the freeze keep. The mount into the agent's HOME is the stated design (`:79-82`) and is not counted here, but it means the agent under test and every `.claude/` hook of the mounted tree can read the operator's codex token during the run.
- **Fix:** Create `meta/home` under a `mktemp -d` outside the run tree (or on `--tmpfs`) and bind-mount that, so an orphaned HOME is not archived with the run; have `run-arms.sh`/the batch runner sweep `meta/home` of any run with `status: running` at start; and surface `CREDS_HOME` copies in `pipeline.json` so an operator can see when they were made.
- **Reference:** CWE-312 Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/312.html; CWE-459 Incomplete Cleanup — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/459.html

### [MED-002] Exit-code taxonomy misclassifies OOM kills and docker-client failures (review Observation 4, confirmed)
- **Severity:** MEDIUM (confidence: medium)
- **File:** `head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:857-862` (`--memory 4g` at `:688`)
- **Issue:** A phase exiting 137 before its timeout is `interrupted` (exit 4). Under `--memory 4g` a container OOM-kill is also 137, so an OOM'd run is excluded from the analysis (`ablation-2.0.yaml:83` excludes `interrupted`) instead of counted. A docker-client failure (exit 125: daemon down, bad flag) reaches `:862` as `agent_error "phase … exited 125"`, charging the arm for an infrastructure fault. The pre-registered rules depend on this taxonomy.
- **Fix:** Keep the container (`--cidfile`, drop `--rm`, remove after inspect) and read `docker inspect --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}}'`; map OOM → `agent_error`/`cap_failure`, 125 → `infrastructure_error`.
- **Reference:** CWE-754 Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
